fair_value.method: Blend of NTM EV/EBITDA (5.75x on ~$740M forward EBITDA at a $6.00/lb copper / $4,000/oz gold deck), P/E (9x ~$4.20 forward EPS), SOTP (producing assets at 5x EBITDA plus Furnas risked at 35% of its $2.0B PEA NPV) and FCF yield (9% on ~$3.19/sh), less ~$150M net debt expected by Q3 2027; ~106.5M diluted shares.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Forward (Q4'27-Q3'28) EBITDA ~$740M: Cu ~80-85kt (2027 guide 75-85kt, 2028 80-90kt) x $6.00/lb x ~95% payable, C1 ~$2.20/lb; Xavantina ~55koz mined + stockpile oz at $4,000/oz, AISC ~$2,300; G&A/royalties ~$95M. 5.75x (mid-tier copper producer range 5-7x; Brazil single-country discount) = EV $4.26B less net debt ~$0.15B = $4.10B / 106.5M sh.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Forward EPS ~$4.20 (EBITDA $740M - D&A ~$150M - interest ~$35M, ~17% effective tax incl. SUDENE incentives, 106.5M sh); 2026E consensus ~C$4.74 (~US$3.36) as cross-check. Multiple 9.0x.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Caraiba+Tucuma+Xavantina at 5.0x forward EBITDA $740M = $3.70B; Furnas at 35% of PEA after-tax NPV8 $2.0B (at $4.60/lb Cu LT) = $0.70B (PFS 2027, FID 2029); exploration incl. Odin Cu-Ni $0.10B; less net debt $0.15B = $4.35B / 106.5M sh.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 FCF ~$340M (EBITDA ~$700M at $6.00 Cu - capex ~$250-280M - cash tax ~$70M - interest ~$40M) = ~$3.19/sh; capitalised at a 9% FCF yield.

bear.story: Copper retraces from ~$6.6/lb record toward $4.9-5.2/lb (Goldman's 2027 $10,750/t view) as tariff front-loading unwinds and LME stocks rebuild; Pilar external shaft slips into 2028 and Caraiba grades stay ~0.9%; BRL strengthens past hedge floors. Forward EBITDA ~$450M x 5x less higher net debt -> ~$20-24.

base.story: Copper holds $5.75-6.50/lb; Ero delivers 2026 guidance (67.5-77.5kt) and guides 2027 at 75-85kt, Tucuma reaches ~4Mtpa with filtration expansion, Pilar shaft commissioned in 2027; net debt falls toward ~$150M and capital returns begin. Stock re-rates only modestly on 5.5-6x forward EBITDA.

bull.story: Structural deficit pushes copper to $7+/lb (Citi $15,000/t call), Pilar ramps on schedule toward 3Mtpa, Furnas PFS in 2027 comes in large and high grade, Ero initiates dividend/buyback; forward EBITDA ~$950M x 6x, net cash -> $55-60.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$25 (about -34%) the market would be discounting either copper sustainably under ~$5/lb or a company-specific failure (Pilar shaft delay/cost overrun, Tucuma throughput/filtration problems, Brazil fiscal or permitting shock) that pushes 2027-28 output below the 75-90kt outlook; at that level forward EV/EBITDA would be <4x on the current deck, which is not ordinary volatility.

catalysts.event: Copper macro: US refined-copper tariff decision / White House stance; LME inventory trend after record $14,875/t on Sep 10
Q3 2026 operating and financial results (H2-weighted production, C1 cost decline at Caraiba, further debt repayment)
Completion of Tucuma tailings filtration expansion targeting ~4Mtpa run-rate
FY2026 production vs 67.5-77.5kt guidance and formal 2027 guidance (outlook 75-85kt Cu, 50-60koz Au) plus capex
FY2026 financials, reserves/resources update incl. Tucuma reserve report; possible capital-return framework
Pilar Mine new external shaft commissioning (Deepening Extension, ramp toward ~3Mtpa ore)
End of historic gold concentrate stockpile sales at Xavantina (low-cost ounces roll off)

key_uncertainties: Copper price path: stock is ~2x levered to copper, which sits near a record (~$6.6/lb) while bank forecasts for 2027 range from ~$4.9/lb (Goldman) to ~$6.8/lb (Citi)
Timing and ramp of the Pilar external shaft, the single biggest driver of 2027-28 Caraiba growth
Tucuma sustaining higher throughput as grades decline; filtration capacity
USD/BRL: hedges floor at 5.54 cover ~70% of 2026 costs; a stronger BRL raises costs beyond the hedge book
Xavantina mined-gold ramp (tracking low end of guidance) and roll-off of stockpile ounces by mid-2027
Capital allocation: timing of dividends/buybacks vs Furnas spending ahead of 2029 FID
reasoning: Ero Copper (NYSE/TSX: ERO) is a Brazil-focused copper producer (Caraiba, Tucuma) with a gold mine (Xavantina) and the Furnas Cu-Au project. Q2 2026 was strong: revenue $284M, adj. EBITDA $144M, adj. EPS $0.83, CFO $138M, net debt down to $453M (0.8x) with another $25M repaid after quarter-end; 2026 Cu guidance 67.5-77.5kt at C1 $2.15-2.35/lb reaffirmed, with H2 weighting. The Feb-2026 outlook calls for 75-85kt in 2027 and 80-90kt in 2028, driven by Tucuma filtration and the Pilar shaft (2027). The Sep-14 Capital Markets Day added cost savings (OneEro, >$20M TC/RC savings) and Furnas (PEA NPV8 $2.0B at $4.60 Cu, PFS 2027, FID 2029). The 102% 1-year move largely reflects copper at records (~$14,600/t, ~$6.6/lb on Sep 23; realized $5.78 in Q2) and gold ~$4,280. At $37.87 (~$4.0B mkt cap, EV ~$4.4B) the stock trades ~5.5x forward EBITDA at spot copper and ~6.3x at my $6.00 deck, so it is roughly fairly priced on spot and slightly rich if copper mean-reverts. My blended fair value (EV/EBITDA, P/E, SOTP with risked Furnas, FCF yield) is ~$38.6, essentially the current price; analyst targets cluster C$45-56 (US$32-40, consensus ~C$48). So I centre the distribution near $38.5 (P(>=38) ~0.51), with no strong drift. For dispersion I used a lognormal with ~48% sigma, below the 64% realized vol because the realized figure is inflated by a one-directional rally, but well above large-cap base rates (+/-25-35%) since the equity is ~2x levered to copper and to a single-country, single-shaft growth plan; I fattened the left tail slightly for copper-crash/Brazil/operational risk. Scenario mean (25% at $22, 50% at $39, 25% at $58) is ~$39.5, consistent with the ladder. Research relied on company filings on sec.gov, news summaries and analyst-target aggregators; no option data was used.
